statement_en: Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain an infinitely connected subgraph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$?

namespace SimpleGraph
open Finset List
variable {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}
def InternallyDisjoint {u v x y : V} (p : G.Walk u v) (q : G.Walk x y) : Prop :=
  Disjoint p.support.tail.dropLast q.support.tail.dropLast
end SimpleGraph

namespace SimpleGraph
open Finset List
variable {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}
def InfinitelyConnected (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop := Nontrivial V ∧
  Pairwise fun u v ↦ ∃ P : Set (G.Walk u v),
    P.Infinite ∧ (∀ p ∈ P, p.IsPath) ∧ P.Pairwise InternallyDisjoint
end SimpleGraph

namespace SimpleGraph
variable {V : Type*}
structure Cycle (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  
  base : V
  
  walk : G.Walk base base
  
  isCycle : walk.IsCycle
end SimpleGraph

namespace SimpleGraph
variable {V : Type*}
def Cycle.edges {G : SimpleGraph V} (c : Cycle G) : List (Sym2 V) := c.walk.edges
end SimpleGraph

open Cardinal Set
structure ThreeUniformHypergraph (V : Type) where
  
  edges : Set (Finset V)
  
  uniform : ∀ e ∈ edges, e.card = 3

namespace ThreeUniformHypergraph
open Cardinal Set
def IsProperColoring {V : Type} (H : ThreeUniformHypergraph V) {C : Type} (f : V → C) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ H.edges, ∃ u ∈ e, ∃ v ∈ e, f u ≠ f v
end ThreeUniformHypergraph

namespace ThreeUniformHypergraph
open Cardinal Set
noncomputable def chromaticCardinal {V : Type} (H : ThreeUniformHypergraph V) : Cardinal.{0} :=
  sInf {κ : Cardinal.{0} | ∃ (C : Type), #C = κ ∧ ∃ f : V → C, H.IsProperColoring f}
end ThreeUniformHypergraph

open Cardinal SimpleGraph

theorem erdos_58505 :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 →
      ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧ InfinitelyConnected H.coe := by
  sorry
